title: Angular momentum splitter effect of $d$-wave axial phonons in orbital altermagnets
abstract: We theoretically demonstrate that axial phonons, lattice vibration quanta carrying finite angular momentum, can host a $d$-wave angular momentum texture in orbital altermagnets in the absence of spin-orbit coupling. We consider a minimal electronic tight-binding model with $d$-wave loop-current order that breaks time-reversal symmetry. Within the Born-Oppenheimer approximation, we incorporate electron-phonon coupling via the molecular Berry curvature and show that the underlying $d$-wave orbital magnetic moment texture of the electronic state is transferred to the phonons without requiring the relativistic spin-orbit coupling. Our results expand the range of platforms available for engineering axial phonons and point to functionality unique to $d$-wave textures, including angular-momentum Seebeck and splitter effects, corresponding to longitudinal and transverse angular-momentum currents driven by a temperature gradient.
summary: The paper theoretically proves that axial phonons can acquire a d-wave angular momentum texture in orbital altermagnets using only electronic structure effects (via the molecular Berry curvature). This bypasses the need for spin-orbit coupling, opening new avenues to engineer exotic phonon functionalities like angular-momentum Seebeck effects.
main_problem: To theoretically demonstrate that axial phonons can host a d-wave angular momentum texture in orbital altermagnets without relying on spin-orbit coupling.
main_result: The authors show the electronic state's d-wave orbital magnetic moment texture is transferred to the lattice vibrations (phonons) via the molecular Berry curvature, enabling new platforms for engineering axial phonons.
method: The study employs the Born-Oppenheimer approximation and analyzes phonon dynamics by diagonalizing an effective Hamiltonian derived from electron-phonon coupling mediated by the Molecular Berry Curvature (MBC).
model_or_system: The system is an orbital altermagnet on a checkerboard lattice, modeled with a minimal tight-binding Hamiltonian exhibiting d-wave loop-current order that breaks time-reversal symmetry.
key_observables: Axial phonons carrying finite angular momentum; the $d$-wave orbital magnetic moment texture ($m_{z,k}$); and measurable effects like angular-momentum Seebeck and splitter effects.
important_parameters: The analysis is restricted to the insulating regime (V=0) and relies on the presence of d-wave symmetry breaking in the electronic state.
main_assumptions: Key approximations include using the Born-Oppenheimer approximation, assuming a minimal tight-binding model, and utilizing Slater determinant forms for basis states.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the orbital almagnet structure on the lattice, the momentum-resolved orbital magnetic moment texture ($m_{z,k}$), and the calculated Molecular Berry Curvature ($	ext{G}_{\alpha\kappa eta}(\mathbf{k})$) in momentum space.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the electronic model and its d-wave texture to calculating the MBC using the BO approximation. It then applies this MBC to derive the phonon Hamiltonian, culminating in the diagonalization of the effective Hamiltonian to predict measurable phonon splitting effects.
why_interesting: This work connects orbital magnetism (a strongly correlated electron phenomenon) directly to lattice dynamics via Berry curvature, providing a mechanism for engineering quantized angular momentum transport in materials without needing relativistic SOC terms.
